classification.difficultyReason: Derive a general formula through three guided stages combining subtraction of cone volumes, axial similarity and rearrangement, then factorisation/substitution. Goals scaffold the route but the symbolic connections exceed routine numerical application.

content.prompt: The portion of a right cone remaining after a smaller cone is cut off it is called a frustum. Suppose that the top and bottom are circles of radius $r$ and $R$, respectively. Also, suppose that the height of the frustum is $h$ and the height of the original cone is $H$.

spec.description: Complete original cone retained above and below its horizontal circular cut. Rear arcs are dashed; front arcs and silhouette are solid. No face shading is needed.
spec.mathematics: Original height H, frustum height h, cut radius r and base radius R. The removed cone has height H-h.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Show that the volume $V$ of the frustum is $\dfrac13\pi\left[H(R^2-r^2)+r^2h\right]$.

answer.short:
$V=\dfrac13\pi\left[H(R^2-r^2)+r^2h\right]$.

Subtract the smaller cone, of height $H-h$, from the original cone.
answer.worked:
The removed cone has radius $r$ and height $H-h$.

$$\begin{align*}V&=\frac13\pi R^2H-\frac13\pi r^2(H-h)\\V&=\frac13\pi\left(R^2H-r^2H+r^2h\right)\\V&=\frac13\pi\left[H(R^2-r^2)+r^2h\right]\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Use similar triangles to show that $H=\dfrac{hR}{R-r}$.

answer.worked:
The axial triangles of the smaller and original cones are similar.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{r}{R}&=\frac{H-h}{H}\\rH&=R(H-h)\\rH&=RH-Rh\\H(R-r)&=Rh\\H&=\frac{hR}{R-r}\end{align*}$$

answer.short:
$V=\dfrac13\pi h(R^2+r^2+rR)$.

Substitute part b into part a and use $R^2-r^2=(R-r)(R+r)$.
answer.worked:
Substitute the result of part b into part a.

$$\begin{align*}V&=\frac13\pi\left[\frac{hR}{R-r}(R^2-r^2)+r^2h\right]\\V&=\frac13\pi\left[\frac{hR}{R-r}(R-r)(R+r)+r^2h\right]\\V&=\frac13\pi\left[hR(R+r)+r^2h\right]\\V&=\frac13\pi h(R^2+r^2+rR)\end{align*}$$
